name: Meltdowns
summary: An intense, involuntary response to being overwhelmed — different from a tantrum in that it isn't goal-directed and the child usually can't self-stop it on request.
triggers: Sensory overload (loud noise, bright light, crowded spaces)
Unexpected changes to routine or transitions
Communication frustration when needs aren't understood
Fatigue, hunger, or illness lowering tolerance

remedies.text: Move to a quieter, dimmer space and reduce sensory input rather than trying to talk the child out of it
Use a visual schedule ahead of transitions so changes are predictable
Deep pressure (weighted blanket, firm hug if welcomed) to help with sensory regulation
